accent.name: a Lua name can't contain accented letters (“{word}”): {hint}

unterminated.double: unfinished string: the closing " is missing (for several lines, use [[ ... ]])
unterminated.single: unfinished string: the closing ' is missing (for several lines, use [[ ... ]])

char.neq: “not equal” is written ~= in Lua, not !=
char.not: “not” is written not in Lua, not !
char.tilde: “~” alone doesn't exist: “not equal” is written ~=
char.and: “and” is written and in Lua, not &&
char.or: “or” is written or in Lua, not ||
char.backtick: “`” doesn't exist in Lua: use " or '

lint.endExpected: “end” expected to close {opener} on line {line}, found {found}
lint.noContinue: Lua has no “continue”: put the rest of the loop in an if
lint.reserved: “{word}” is a Lua reserved word: it can't be used as a name ({what})
lint.noLabel: no visible label “::{name}::” for this goto
lint.gotoScope: the goto on line {line} jumps into the scope of local variable “{name}”: declare it before the goto
lint.lastStatement: “{word}” must be the last statement of its block (before “end”, “else” or “until”)

what.label: label
what.forBounds: between the start and the end of the for loop

lint.forIn: “=” or “in” expected after the for loop variable, found {found}
lint.assignCall: you can't assign a value to the result of a function call
lint.assignExpr: this expression can't receive a value
lint.compound: Lua has no “{op}=” operator: write x = x {bin} value
lint.concatAssign: Lua has no “..=” operator: write s = s .. value
lint.compareNotAssign: “==” compares two values; to assign, use a single =
lint.incomplete: incomplete statement: a function call or an assignment (=) is expected
lint.incompleteFound: incomplete statement: a function call or an assignment (=) is expected, found {found}
lint.floorDiv: Lua 5.1 has no “//” operator: use math.floor(a / b)
lint.vararg: “...” can only be used in a function declared with “...” in its parameters
lint.tableClose: “}” expected to close the table opened on line {line} (separate the items with commas), found {found}
lint.undefinedHint: “{name}” is not defined: did you mean “{hint}”?
lint.undefined: “{name}” is not defined (variable never assigned nor declared with local)
lint.colonCall: write {base}.{name}(...) with a dot: “:” would pass {base} as the first argument
lint.parenLine: this “(” at the start of a line continues the call on the previous line; add “;” at the end of the previous line if that's not intended
lint.exprEof: expression expected, but the script ends there
lint.exprEnd: unexpected “end”: an expression is missing before it, or there is an extra “end”
lint.exprKeyword: expression expected, found the reserved word “{word}”
lint.exprEquals: unexpected “=”: a value is missing before it, or to compare use ==
lint.callClose: “)” expected to close the call opened on line {line} (separate the arguments with commas), found {found}
